novelty.justification: The claim’s novelty route is a mechanism/measurement hypothesis: “the same shared-init geometry that enables transmission also enables detection,” with detectability declining as the reference model diverges from the teacher’s base. Searches for “subliminal learning same base model detection,” “hidden trait transmission gradient alignment auditor,” and “same initialization covert trait detector” identify Cloud et al., “Subliminal Learning: Language models transmit behavioral traits via hidden signals in data” (2025; published in Nature in 2026), as the closest work because it already establishes shared-base-dependent transmission and failure of generic detection; AGPD (2023) is also methodologically adjacent in using activation gradients to detect poisoned samples. Turning the known transmission asymmetry into a same-base auditor and predicting a coupled detectability-versus-divergence curve is a natural extension rather than a new paradigm, but it is a non-trivial operationalization not contained in the closest work; the gradient-alignment and probe components themselves are standard methods rather than novel measurement principles.
